why: U9 / flagstaff R8. The claim is that `schema.json` plus one worked example is enough for an agent to write a working flagstaff plugin in one turn, and that `flagstaff check` tells it so without a human reading the output. Both halves are the hypothesis: if the agent needs a second turn, or needs someone to explain the refusal, the schema is not self-describing and `check` is not the feedback loop it is meant to be. Measured here rather than asserted in the design.
prompt: Read packages/flagstaff/src/schema.json and packages/flagstaff/README.md. Write a flagstaff plugin to the file evals/results/pulse-plugin.mjs. It must be a single ES module with a default export, must be named "pulse", and must contribute one spinner style also called "pulse" with at least three frames. Then verify it by running: node packages/flagstaff/dist/cli.js check evals/results/pulse-plugin.mjs — and if that command exits non-zero, fix the plugin until it exits zero. Do not modify anything under packages/.

expect.value: node packages/flagstaff/dist/cli.js check evals/results/pulse-plugin.mjs | grep -q '^pulse: ok'
node packages/flagstaff/dist/cli.js check evals/results/pulse-plugin.mjs | grep -qE '^  pipe .*[^ ]'
